# SQL

Format SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, CTEs and DDL.

Category: Formatters · ID: `sql-format` · Search terms: sql, query, postgres, mysql, sqlite, beautify, pretty

## Command line

```bash
devtooltui sql-format [file|-] [flags]
```

## Inputs

1. Input

## Options

| Flag | Values | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--indent` | 1–8 | `2` | Indent. |
| `--uppercase` | on/off | `true` | Uppercase keywords. |

## Examples

From the tests (`testdata/sql-format`), so they are what the tool prints.

### cte

Input:

```text
WITH recent AS (SELECT id, total FROM orders WHERE created_at > now() - interval '7 days'), big AS (select * from recent where total > 100) SELECT r.id, (SELECT count(*) FROM big) AS big_count FROM recent r WHERE r.id IN (1, 2, 3) OR r.total::numeric > 50;
```

Output:

```text
WITH recent AS (
  SELECT
    id,
    total
  FROM
    orders
  WHERE
    created_at > now() - INTERVAL '7 days'
),
big AS (
  SELECT
    *
  FROM
    recent
  WHERE
    total > 100
)
SELECT
  r.id,
  (
    SELECT
      count(*)
    FROM
      big
  ) AS big_count
FROM
  recent r
WHERE
  r.id IN (1, 2, 3)
  OR r.total::numeric > 50;
```

### dml

Input:

```text
insert into users (id, email, name) values (1, 'ana@example.com', 'Ana'), (2, 'bob@example.com', 'O''Brien') on conflict (id) do update set email = excluded.email returning id;
update users set name = 'Ana P.', updated_at = now() where id = 1;
delete from sessions where expires_at < now() /* stale */;
create table orders (id bigint primary key, customer_id bigint not null references customers(id), total numeric(10, 2) default 0, created_at timestamptz);
```

Output:

```text
INSERT INTO users (id, email, name)
VALUES
  (1, 'ana@example.com', 'Ana'),
  (2, 'bob@example.com', 'O''Brien')
ON CONFLICT (id) DO UPDATE
SET
  email = excluded.email
RETURNING
  id;

UPDATE users
SET
  name = 'Ana P.',
  updated_at = now()
WHERE
  id = 1;

DELETE FROM sessions
WHERE
  expires_at < now() /* stale */;

CREATE TABLE orders (
  id bigint PRIMARY KEY,
  customer_id bigint NOT NULL REFERENCES customers(id),
  total numeric(10, 2) DEFAULT 0,
  created_at timestamptz
);
```

### select

Input:

```text
-- active customers with their last order
select c.id, c.name, count(o.id) as orders, max(o.created_at) last_order from customers c left join orders o on o.customer_id = c.id and o.status <> 'cancelled' where c.active = true and c.created_at between '2026-01-01' and now() group by c.id, c.name having count(o.id) > 2 order by orders desc, c.name limit 10;
```

Output:

```text
-- active customers with their last order
SELECT
  c.id,
  c.name,
  count(o.id) AS orders,
  max(o.created_at) last_order
FROM
  customers c
LEFT JOIN orders o
  ON o.customer_id = c.id
  AND o.status <> 'cancelled'
WHERE
  c.active = TRUE
  AND c.created_at BETWEEN '2026-01-01' AND now()
GROUP BY
  c.id,
  c.name
HAVING
  count(o.id) > 2
ORDER BY
  orders DESC,
  c.name
LIMIT 10;
```
